themes_detail.label: Noise complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints spiked to 52 this week across CD406, a 427% jump versus the 9.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden and significant quality-of-life deterioration for residents.
evidence: 52 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (427% increase, z-score: 7.61)
Park noise complaints also elevated: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (900% spike, z-score: 6.36)
Sustained multi-week signal suggests systemic problem, not isolated incident
reporting_angles: Canvass affected residents in high-complaint zones (subway noise, construction, nightlife districts) to understand source and duration
NYPD data: are noise enforcement actions keeping pace with complaint volume, or is backlog growing?

themes_detail.label: Obstruction complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped 482% this past week (8 complaints vs. 1.4 weekly average), indicating a sudden surge in blocked sidewalks, driveways, or public right-of-way issues affecting pedestrian and vehicle access.
evidence: 8 obstruction complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (482% increase, z-score: 7.73)
Complements existing high volume of blocked driveway complaints (570 total over 90 days)
Sharp single-week spike suggests event-driven problem or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Investigate specific locations of obstruction complaints to identify pattern (construction sites, vendor clusters, parking violations)
SanDep/DOT enforcement: are street sweeps or parking enforcement operations on hold or reallocated?

themes_detail.label: Tree hazards multiply
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints (4 this week vs. 0.5 weekly average, 700% increase) and overgrown branch complaints (5 last week vs. 0.6 average, 700% increase) signal rapid deterioration of street tree stock, creating safety and quality-of-life risks.
evidence: Dead/dying tree complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 4.95)
Overgrown tree/branch complaints: 5 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 6.29)
Community board budget requests repeatedly ask for park and amenity improvements, suggesting infrastructure maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Parks Dept inventory: are tree inspection and removal schedules keeping up with aging street canopy in Forest Hills/Rego Park?
Interview residents about branch falls, storm damage, or pest infestations that may have triggered spike
Tie to broader urban forest management story—are species losses accelerating citywide?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/vaping complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints surged to 9 last week, a 700% jump versus the 1.1 weekly baseline, suggesting either new problem behavior or shift in resident reporting of indoor air quality violations.
evidence: 9 smoking/vaping complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 7.48)
Isolated spike without long-term trend context—pattern unclear
reporting_angles: Locate complaint clusters by address type (apartments, businesses, parks) to determine if issue is indoor air quality, secondhand smoke in common areas, or illegal smoking ordinance violations
NYPD/DOH enforcement: are smoking violations being actively pursued in Forest Hills/Rego Park?

themes_detail.label: Dangling street signs hazard
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints jumped to 10 complaints two weeks ago, a 433% spike versus the 1.9 weekly average, creating potential safety hazards and signaling deferred infrastructure maintenance.
evidence: 10 dangling street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% increase, z-score: 5.59)
Broader pattern: street condition complaints total 785 over 90 days, indicating persistent infrastructure neglect
DOT/DCP budget requests in community board history suggest ongoing maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: DOT data: what is the backlog for sign repair/replacement citywide and in Queens?
Visual audit: canvass Forest Hills/Rego Park for other deferred infrastructure (potholes, curb damage, missing signage)
